newsitem.title: TRINIDAD AND TOBAGO: U.S. drug agency to open office in Trinidad.
newsitem.headline: U.S. drug agency to open office in Trinidad.

text.p: The U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration will open an office in Trinidad to help local police curb illegal trafficking, Prime Minister Basdeo Panday said.
Panday, speaking to reporters late Thursday after a trip to the United States and Canada, said that drug traffickers had infiltrated legitimate businesses, including the news media.
"I was amazed by the volume of information the U.S. government has on the drug dealers and traffickers in Trinidad and Tobago," he said.

"They shared some of that information with me and you will be amazed to know how deep the drug lords have infiltrated into what appears to be legitimate business, including the media," Panday said. He did not elaborate.
Panday said he was confident that Washington would address Trinidad's request for North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA) parity status after the November election.
